nodes.label: Configuration System
nodes.rationale: Layered merge pattern: global settings (~/.jarvis/settings.json) → project overrides (.jarvis/settings.json) → environment variables → runtime config. JSON chosen over YAML/TOML for universal parseability, nested structure support, and flexible overridability without requiring env vars for every option.

nodes.label: Single-Agent Architecture Design
nodes.rationale: Single JarvisV2 agent with rich tool set avoids coordination overhead, context fragmentation, and failure modes of multi-agent systems. Tools encapsulate agent-like behavior (sub-agent delegation via `agents` tool, MCP adapters, skill activation) without agent-to-agent handoff complexity.

nodes.label: Lazy MCP Architecture
nodes.rationale: Single `mcp` proxy tool (~200 tokens) instead of registering every individual MCP tool (~150-300 tokens each). Lazy connections: servers connect only on first tool call. Offline discovery via metadata cache enables search/describe without live connections. Reduces token usage from 10k+ to ~200.

nodes.label: WebUI Design Token System
nodes.rationale: Centralized CSS custom properties (RGB channel variables) in globals.css `:root` with 25 reusable component classes. Eliminated ~400+ hardcoded rgba() values across 30 component files. Theme by changing RGB values in ONE file — everything cascades. Variables use per-channel format (--brand-r/g/b) for arbitrary alpha opacity.

nodes.label: System Prompt Optimization
nodes.rationale: Rewrote all prompts using Markdown + XML hybrid format. Markdown for readable structure (headings, lists, tables), XML tags for critical constraints. Removed narrative fluff, combined behaviors into single directives. Total reduction: ~4,872 → ~4,125 tokens (15%).

nodes.label: Safety Profiles
nodes.rationale: 5 safety levels (Lockdown/Restricted/Balanced/Permissive/Unrestricted) cycling via Shift+Tab. Each level sets code execution, file ops, and dangerous ops permissions independently. Enforced through permission manager with global bypass, tool-level config, and granular path-based rules.

nodes.label: Reusable CSS Component Classes
nodes.rationale: 25 reusable .techy-* CSS classes defined in @layer components in globals.css covering panels, dialogs, buttons, text, bubbles, layout, and badges. Prefer CSS classes over inline styles for common UI patterns.

nodes.label: Behavioral Guidelines for LLM Agents
nodes.rationale: Four principles: Think Before Coding (surface tradeoffs, state assumptions), Simplicity First (minimum code, no speculation), Surgical Changes (touch only what you must, clean up own mess), Goal-Driven Execution (define success criteria, loop until verified). Bias toward caution over speed.

nodes.label: Design: Single-Agent Architecture
nodes.rationale: Simplicity and reliability. A single agent with rich tool set avoids coordination overhead, context fragmentation, and failure modes of multi-agent systems.

nodes.label: Design: SDKAdapter Pattern
nodes.rationale: Provider independence. SDKAdapter normalizes typed SDK interface into dict-based contract. Adding a new provider only requires implementing BaseLLMSDK.

nodes.label: Design: Operations Protocol Pattern
nodes.rationale: Testability and extensibility. Typing.Protocols enable runtime backend swapping without changing tool implementations.

nodes.label: Design: EventBus + HookRegistry Pattern
nodes.rationale: Decoupling. EventBus allows any number of subscribers without agent loop awareness. HookRegistry gives extensions control (block/modify) not just observation.

nodes.label: Design: Python Extensions via importlib
nodes.rationale: Zero barrier to entry. Any Python developer can write an extension without learning a new API format. importlib loading means extensions are just .py files.

nodes.label: Design: JSON Config Files
nodes.rationale: Simplicity + overridability. JSON is universally parseable, supports nested structures, and layered merge gives flexible setup without env vars for every option.

nodes.label: Design: Progressive Skill Disclosure
nodes.rationale: Context window efficiency. Only name/description/when_to_use shown in system prompt; full content loads on demand via activate_skill tool.

nodes.label: Design: MCP Tools as BaseTool Instances
nodes.rationale: Uniform tool interface. Wrapping MCP tools as BaseTool lets existing tool dispatch, permission checking, and callback infrastructure work identically.
nodes.norm_label: design: mcp tools as basetool instances

nodes.label: Design: Heartbeat Disabled by Default
nodes.rationale: User autonomy. Periodic background awareness is powerful but surprising. Users opt in via config.

nodes.label: Markdown + XML Hybrid Prompt Format
nodes.rationale: Markdown for readable structure, XML tags for critical constraints. Achieved ~15% token reduction (4,872 to 4,125 tokens) across all agent prompts.
